changes: About $325mn of the $980.8mn was one-off 'asset-light' revenue; without it revenue grew ~13% QoQ, not 68% (6-K ex. 99.2; our calc).

Delivery slipped: New Jersey (Microsoft) will have 'more than half' of contracted capacity by year-end, the rest in 2Q27, after temporary generation was retired early; FY26 revenue goes to the low end and $7bn ARR moves to February.
First 2027 guide: revenue $12-13bn (consensus ~$12.2bn) but capex $40-45bn, 75-85% from prepayments and asset-backed debt, pre-tax breakeven only in 4Q27.

Prepayments are now the funding model: >90% of 3Q contract value carries one, covering >100% of related capex; deferred revenue rose $3.43bn to $9.41bn, but receivables rose $3.76bn and 3Q operating cash flow was -$273mn.

Debt rose to $14.19bn from $8.55bn (converts $5.75bn, $775mn asset-backed facility); operating cash flow swung from +$2.25bn in 2Q to -$273mn; the $3.5bn Citi secured facility (October) was not addressed on the call.

consensus_thesis: Investors own Nebius for hyperscaler-anchored demand, a ~40% EBITDA margin and prepayment-heavy funding; at $154.69 on 11 November (about $123 intraday on 12 November, -20%, Investing.com) the market prices delivery and funding risk, not demand.
headline: The consensus view should shift from 'demand-led compounding' to 'execution and funding': demand and pricing (>$25mn per MW-year) look stronger, but delivery slips, a much larger 2027 capex bill and uncollected prepayments mean credit quality holds only if 2027 prepayments of $17-20bn are collected on time.
kona: Nebius now gets >90% of new contract value prepaid and says prepayments cover all related capex, at >$25mn per MW-year: Kona should ask GPU-cloud or hosting tenants for prepayments sized to capex, not just deposits. The Vineland delay came from temporary generation being retired early, so behind-the-meter power is now a tenant-facing delivery risk: Kona should show permanent gas generation and fuel supply fully contracted before committing dates, and price delay credits. Collection matters as much as signing: tie prepayment due dates to construction draws.

sections.body: Emphasized more: prepayments as standard terms, contract value per MW, 2027 capacity (>1 GW a year) and a switch to revenue and pre-tax guidance. Less or dropped: ARR ('no longer the right measure'), connected-MW targets, the 800 MW-1 GW year-end goal. KPIs more important: deferred revenue and receivables, pre-tax income, RPO. Risks up: delivery at colocation sites, funding scale. Down: demand and pricing. → Dropping ARR the quarter it slips, and not disclosing MW, reduces the market's ability to track delivery; deferred revenue and receivables become the best proxy.

What the next dollar costs: secured asset-backed debt at SOFR+250bp (July) and the Citi bridge at SOFR+275bp stepping to 350bp; converts cheap but convert at about $313-325 (preview), far above the share price. Maturities in 24 months: the Citi facility (364-day from October per preview; draw undisclosed). Management cites payback under two years on five-year deals with prepayments covering over 100% of capex: the risk is timing and collection, not pricing. Issued shares rose more than the ATM alone explains (+21mn QoQ in issued shares), so check the 6-K share bridge. → 2027 needs $40-45bn; if prepayments of $17-20bn arrive on time and asset-backed debt covers most of the rest, equity need is small; a slip of one quarter in collections widens the gap by several billion.
